ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating KL Regularization via Trajectory Embeddings
PROPOSAL: We propose using trajectory embeddings to estimate the KL divergence between the fine-tuned and pre-trained distributions, circumventing the intractability of marginal likelihoods. Specifically, we will pre-train a model to embed each denoising trajectory into a low-dimensional space, where the KL divergence can be approximated using the embedding distances. We will then fine-tune the diffusion model using the regularized reward maximization objective with the KL regularization term approximated by the trajectory embeddings.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with the current state-of-the-art approaches of ignoring the KL term, using the trajectory KL constraint, and rejection sampling methods (RSO, RAFT, and Reinforce-Rej). We will also ablate the quality of the trajectory embeddings on fine-tuning results.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should improve upon the trajectory KL constraint method and offer a more efficient alternative to ignoring the KL term, but it may fail if the low-dimensional embeddings do not capture the relevant information for fine-tuning.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating KL Regularization via Trajectory Embeddings
PROPOSAL: We propose using trajectory embeddings to estimate the KL divergence between the fine-tuned and pre-trained distributions, circumventing the intractability of marginal likelihoods. Specifically, we will pre-train a model to embed each denoising trajectory into a low-dimensional space, where the KL divergence can be approximated using the embedding distances. To further improve the quality of the trajectory embeddings, we will also pre-train a separate model to predict the reward from the embedding space. The predicted reward will be used to adjust the KL regularization term, allowing for more informed fine-tuning. We will then fine-tune the diffusion model using the regularized reward maximization objective with the KL regularization term approximated by the trajectory embeddings and adjusted by the predicted reward.
CONTROLS: The same as before. We will also investigate the impact of the reward predictor's architecture and quality on fine-tuning results.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to better fine-tuning results compared to our previous revision, especially for tasks with well-defined rewards, but it may fail if the reward predictor overfits or does not capture the relevant information for fine-tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Integrating Diffusion Model Structure for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose incorporating the diffusion model's generative structure into the fine-tuning process by using a multi-step predictor that predicts the reward at each denoising step. The multi-step predictor will be trained to alleviate the initial value function bias problem, allowing for more effective KL regularization. We will fine-tune the diffusion model using the regularized reward maximization objective with the KL regularization term approximated by the trajectory embeddings proposed in our previous work.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with the sequential application of current state-of-the-art approaches (ignoring the KL term, using the trajectory KL constraint, and rejection sampling methods) and investigate the impact of the multi-step predictor's architecture and quality on fine-tuning results.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should improve upon the sequential application of current methods and offer a more efficient fine-tuning process, but it may fail if the multi-step predictor does not capture the relevant information for fine-tuning or if the fine-tuning process becomes unstable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-Agnostic Correction of Pre-Trained Flow Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a reward-agnostic correction method to address the errors in pre-trained flow models without explicit rewards. The method involves learning a new flow model that corrects the pre-trained model's distribution by iteratively refining the flow layers using the maximum likelihood estimate of the corrected distribution, which is learned from samples from the data distribution. We will use the pre-trained model's reverse process as a starting point and iteratively refine the flow layers to correct the distribution without requiring explicit rewards.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with ignoring the KL term, using the trajectory KL constraint, and rejection sampling methods. We will also investigate the impact of the number of iterations, the flow layer architecture, and the data distribution on the correction results.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to improved sample quality without the need for explicit rewards, but it may fail if the pre-trained model's distribution is not close enough to the target distribution or if the correction process becomes unstable.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: 3. Reward-Agnostic Correction of Pre-Trained Flow Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a reward-agnostic correction method to address the errors in pre-trained flow models without explicit rewards. The method involves learning a new flow model that corrects the pre-trained model's distribution by iteratively refining the flow layers using the maximum likelihood estimate of the corrected distribution, which is learned from samples from the data distribution or generated samples from the pre-trained model. We will use a variant of the pre-trained model's reverse process as a starting point and iteratively refine the flow layers to correct the distribution without requiring explicit rewards. Additionally, we will also explore the use of augmented data distributions to improve the effectiveness of the correction process.
CONTROLS: The same as before. We will also evaluate the impact of different data augmentation techniques and the number of iterations on the correction results.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised approach should lead to improved sample quality without the need for explicit rewards, especially with the addition of augmented data distributions. However, it may fail if the pre-trained model's distribution is not close enough to the target distribution or if the correction process becomes unstable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Best-of-N Sampling for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose applying Best-of-N sampling to diffusion models, which has been shown to improve the quality of generated samples for autoregressive models. We will evaluate the impact of Best-of-N sampling on the fine-tuning of diffusion models and compare it with our previous proposals (Investigating KL Regularization via Trajectory Embeddings and Integrating Diffusion Model Structure for Fine-Tuning).
CONTROLS: We will investigate the effect of different sample sizes (N) and the number of best samples kept on the fine-tuning results. Additionally, we will compare our method with rejection sampling methods (RSO, RAFT, and Reinforce-Rej) and evaluate its performance in text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to improved sample quality, especially when combined with previous methods, but it may fail if the Best-of-N sampling does not effectively capture the underlying distribution or if the fine-tuning process becomes unstable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Effect of Trajectory Length on Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose investigating the effect of trajectory length on the fine-tuning of diffusion models. By shortening or lengthening the denoising process, we can potentially improve the efficiency and stability of the fine-tuning process. We will evaluate the impact of different trajectory lengths on the fine-tuning results and compare it with our previous proposals (Investigating KL Regularization via Trajectory Embeddings, Integrating Diffusion Model Structure for Fine-Tuning, and Reward-Agnostic Correction of Pre-Trained Flow Models).
CONTROLS: We will investigate the effect of different trajectory lengths (shorter and longer than the default length) on the fine-tuning results. Additionally, we will compare our method with rejection sampling methods (RSO, RAFT, and Reinforce-Rej) and evaluate its performance in text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to improved fine-tuning results, especially for tasks where the trajectory length affects the distribution, but it may fail if the fine-tuning process becomes unstable or if the optimal trajectory length is not well-suited for the task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Fine-Tuned Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose evaluating the robustness of fine-tuned diffusion models using adversarial attacks, such as the ones generated by the Procedural Adversarial Network (PAN). By evaluating the robustness of fine-tuned models, we can assess their generalization capabilities and identify potential vulnerabilities. We will compare the robustness of fine-tuned models obtained using different methods (Investigating KL Regularization via Trajectory Embeddings, Integrating Diffusion Model Structure for Fine-Tuning, Reward-Agnostic Correction of Pre-Trained Flow Models, and Investigating Best-of-N Sampling for Diffusion Models).
CONTROLS: We will use the PAN to generate adversarial attacks and evaluate the robustness of fine-tuned models using metrics such as the average distance between the clean and adversarial samples. Additionally, we will compare our results with the robustness of models fine-tuned using rejection sampling methods (RSO, RAFT, and Reinforce-Rej).
COST: 60 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should provide valuable insights into the robustness of fine-tuned diffusion models, but it may fail if the adversarial attacks do not capture the relevant information for assessing robustness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Pre-Trained Features for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose investigating the use of pre-trained features for fine-tuning diffusion models. By leveraging pre-trained features, we can potentially improve the fine-tuning process and reduce the need for large amounts of labeled data. We will compare the use of pre-trained features with our previous proposals (Investigating KL Regularization via Trajectory Embeddings, Integrating Diffusion Model Structure for Fine-Tuning, Reward-Agnostic Correction of Pre-Trained Flow Models, Investigating Best-of-N Sampling for Diffusion Models, and Analyzing the Effect of Trajectory Length on Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models) and evaluate their effect on the fine-tuning process.
CONTROLS: We will investigate the effect of different pre-trained feature architectures and the quality of the pre-trained features on the fine-tuning results. Additionally, we will compare our results with rejection sampling methods (RSO, RAFT, and Reinforce-Rej) and evaluate their performance in text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to improved fine-tuning results, especially for tasks where pre-trained features are available, but it may fail if the pre-trained features do not capture the relevant information for the task or if the fine-tuning process becomes unstable.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: 7. Investigating the Use of Pre-Trained Features for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a hybrid approach that combines pre-trained features with our previous proposals (Investigating KL Regularization via Trajectory Embeddings, Integrating Diffusion Model Structure for Fine-Tuning, Reward-Agnostic Correction of Pre-Trained Flow Models, Investigating Best-of-N Sampling for Diffusion Models, Analyzing the Effect of Trajectory Length on Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models, and Evaluating the Robustness of Fine-Tuned Diffusion Models) to fine-tune diffusion models. By leveraging the strengths of both pre-trained features and our previous proposals, we aim to develop a more robust and efficient fine-tuning method. We will evaluate the performance of our hybrid approach on text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our hybrid approach with rejection sampling methods (RSO, RAFT, and Reinforce-Rej) and evaluate the effect of different pre-trained feature architectures and the quality of the pre-trained features on the fine-tuning results.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This hybrid approach should lead to improved fine-tuning results and robustness, especially for tasks where pre-trained features are available, but it may fail if the pre-trained features do not capture the relevant information for the task or if the fine-tuning process becomes unstable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trajectory KL Divergence Relaxation for KL-Regularized Reward Maximization in Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of different approximations of the marginal KL divergence, such as the trajectory KL divergence, with that of ignoring the KL term altogether. Evaluate the proposed methods on a text-to-image generation task using a pre-trained diffusion model and the COCO 2017 dataset. For control, include a baseline of vanilla PPO without KL regularization.
CONTROLS: Vanilla PPO without KL regularization, ignoring the KL term, trajectory KL divergence relaxation with a fixed number of timesteps, and a method to estimate the marginal KL with a known upper bound.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The trajectory KL divergence relaxation will significantly outperform ignoring the KL term, but may not achieve the same stability as the baseline PPO without KL regularization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leverage Intermediate Noisy States for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate fine-tuning diffusion models using a variant of rejection sampling that incorporates information from intermediate noisy states during the denoising process. Train a pre-trained diffusion model on a document layout generation task using theiane dataset and fine-tune it using the proposed method. Evaluate the performance of the fine-tuned model against a baseline of vanilla PPO fine-tuning without access to the intermediate states.
CONTROLS: Vanilla PPO fine-tuning without access to intermediate states, rejection sampling without intermediate state information, and a baseline of no fine-tuning.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will lead to a significant improvement over the baseline in terms of both the quality and the efficiency of generated layouts, but its performance may degrade in cases with significant variabilities in the intermediate states.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning from Data-Driven Noise in Flow Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate correcting errors in pre-trained flow models using a data-driven approach that learns to modify the noise schedule of the model based on samples from the data distribution. Train a pre-trained flow model on a molecule generation task using the ZINC dataset and fine-tune it using the proposed method. Evaluate the performance of the fine-tuned model against a baseline of no fine-tuning and a baseline of traditional KL-regularized PPO fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: No fine-tuning, traditional KL-regularized PPO fine-tuning, and an ablation of the data-driven noise schedule learning.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will lead to a significant improvement over the baseline in terms of the diversity and accuracy of generated molecules, but its performance may degrade in cases with very high-dimensional data distributions.

PROPOSAL: Modify the rejection sampler used in the previous proposal to incorporate a learnable schedule for selecting the intermediate noisy states that are relevant for the task at hand. Train a pre-trained diffusion model on a text-to-image generation task using the COCO 2017 dataset and fine-tune it using the proposed method. Evaluate the performance of the fine-tuned model against the baseline of vanilla PPO fine-tuning without access to intermediate states.
CONTROLS: Vanilla PPO fine-tuning without access to intermediate states, rejection sampling without intermediate state information, and the original baseline of no fine-tuning.
COST: 60 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will lead to a further improvement in the quality and diversity of generated images, and its performance will be more robust to variations in the intermediate states.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Intrinsic Reward Learning for CL-Regularized Reward Maximization in Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate learning intrinsic rewards that can be used to fine-tune diffusion models without explicit human-provided reward feedback. Train a pre-trained diffusion model on a document layout generation task using theiane dataset and learn an intrinsic reward function using the predictive coding framework. Evaluate the performance of the fine-tuned model against a baseline of no fine-tuning and a baseline of traditional KL-regularized PPO fine-tuning with human-provided reward feedback.
CONTROLS: No fine-tuning, traditional KL-regularized PPO fine-tuning with human-provided reward feedback, and an ablation of the intrinsic reward learning.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will lead to a significant improvement over the baseline in terms of the quality and efficiency of generated layouts, but its performance may degrade in cases with very complex task dynamics.

TITLE: Best-of-N Sampling for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the application of Best-of-N sampling for fine-tuning diffusion models, and its connections to policy gradient methods and rejection sampling. Train a pre-trained diffusion model on a molecule generation task using the ZINC dataset and fine-tune it using the proposed method. Evaluate the performance of the fine-tuned model against a baseline of vanilla PPO fine-tuning and a baseline of rejection sampling.
CONTROLS: Vanilla PPO fine-tuning, rejection sampling, and a baseline of no fine-tuning.
COST: 90 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will lead to a significant improvement over the baseline in terms of the diversity and accuracy of generated molecules, and its performance will be comparable to rejection sampling.

TITLE: Time-Sliced Online Learning for Flow Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of time-sliced online learning to fine-tune flow models, where the model is updated in small increments over multiple samples from the data distribution. Train a pre-trained flow model on a text-to-image generation task using the COCO 2017 dataset and fine-tune it using the proposed method. Evaluate the performance of the fine-tuned model against a baseline of traditional KL-regularized PPO fine-tuning and a baseline of no fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Traditional KL-regularized PPO fine-tuning, baseline of no fine-tuning, and an ablation of the time-sliced online learning.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will lead to a significant improvement over the baseline in terms of the quality and efficiency of generated images, and its performance will be more robust to variations in the data distribution.

PROPOSAL: Modify the Best-of-N sampling scheme to incorporate a second-stage reinforcement learning phase, where the sampled sequences are further refined to optimize the reward. Train a pre-trained diffusion model on a document layout generation task using theiane dataset and fine-tune it using the proposed method. Evaluate the performance of the fine-tuned model against a baseline of vanilla PPO fine-tuning and a baseline of rejection sampling.
CONTROLS: Vanilla PPO fine-tuning, rejection sampling, and a baseline of no fine-tuning.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will lead to a significant improvement over the baseline in terms of the quality and efficiency of generated layouts, and its performance will be more robust to variations in the data distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Adapting Pre-Trained Diffusion Models to New Tasks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of meta-learning to adapt pre-trained diffusion models to new tasks, where the model is trained to quickly learn new distributions with few samples. Train a pre-trained diffusion model on a set of diverse tasks and fine-tune it using the proposed method. Evaluate the performance of the fine-tuned model against a baseline of traditional fine-tuning and a baseline of no fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Traditional fine-tuning, baseline of no fine-tuning, and an ablation of the meta-learning.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will lead to a significant improvement over the baseline in terms of the ability to adapt to new tasks with few samples, and its performance will be more robust to variations in the data distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring KL-Regularized Reward Maximization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Implement a KL-regularized reward maximization approach for diffusion models, where we maximize the expected reward while penalizing the KL divergence between the fine-tuned distribution and the pre-trained model, using a relaxation of the marginal KL divergence that upper-bounds the true KL. We will train a vanilla diffusion model on a large text-to-image generation dataset and fine-tune it on a subset of the data using the proposed approach.
CONTROLS: Ablation study to compare the relaxed KL regularization to ignoring the KL term entirely and to the trajectory KL constraint; baseline results using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) without KL regularization.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed method to achieve stable training in large-scale settings and improve sample quality over ignoring the KL term, but may suffer from the initial value function bias problem.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Relaxation on KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experiment where we vary the relaxation strength of the marginal KL divergence in the KL-regularized reward maximization approach and evaluate its effect on the fine-tuned model's performance. Specifically, we will compare the results obtained using different relaxation methods, such as the trajectory KL constraint, the path-KL divergence, and the importance-weighted KL divergence.
CONTROLS: Compare the different relaxation methods to the baseline method where the KL term is ignored entirely; ablation study to understand the impact of relaxation strength on performance.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to show that stronger relaxation of the KL divergence can lead to better performance, but may also introduce bias in the fine-tuned model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Step KL Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel multi-step KL regularization approach for diffusion models, where we apply KL regularization not only at the end of the denoising process but also at intermediate steps. This approach leverages the hierarchical structure of the denoising process and aims to reduce the initial value function bias problem.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed multi-step KL regularization approach to the standard KL-regularized reward maximization approach; ablation study to understand the impact of the number of intermediate regularization steps on performance.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed approach to improve sample quality and stability, especially when processing long sequences or high-dimensional data, but may also increase computational costs due to the additional regularization steps.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Multi-Step KL Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We revise the proposal to explore two different variants of multi-step KL regularization: (1) intermediate KL regularization, where we apply KL regularization at intermediate steps of the denoising process, and (2) hierarchical KL regularization, where we use a coarse-to-fine approach to KL regularization, first at coarse time steps and then at finer time steps. This will allow us to investigate the effects of different regularization strategies on performance.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed multi-step KL regularization approaches to the standard KL-regularized reward maximization approach; ablation study to understand the impact of the number of intermediate regularization steps and the choice of regularization strategy on performance.
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to show that the hierarchical KL regularization approach outperforms the intermediate KL regularization approach, especially when processing long sequences or high-dimensional data, due to its ability to capture finer-grained information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leverage Denoising Process Structure for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose to leverage the structure of the denoising process in diffusion models to improve fine-tuning. Specifically, we will incorporate intermediate denoising steps into the reward function, providing a forward process matching the backward denoising process. This should help alleviate the initial value function bias problem and provide a more natural way to fine-tune diffusion models.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed approach to the standard KL-regularized reward maximization approach; ablation study to understand the impact of incorporating intermediate denoising steps on performance.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to show significant improvement in sample quality and stability, especially when processing long sequences or high-dimensional data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Sequential Sampling on Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effect of sequential sampling strategies on the fine-tuning of diffusion models. Specifically, we compare the performance of batch sampling and sequential sampling (e.g., sampling one sequence at a time) on a set of real-world benchmarks in text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation. We also analyze the impact of different batch sizes and sequence lengths on fine-tuning performance.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of batch sampling and sequential sampling to the standard KL-regularized reward maximization approach; ablation study to understand the impact of different batch sizes and sequence lengths on performance.
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to show that sequential sampling can improve fine-tuning performance, especially for long sequences or high-dimensional data, and to provide insights into the optimal batch size and sequence length for various applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Correcting Pre-Trained Flows Using Unsupervised Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose an unsupervised fine-tuning approach for pre-trained flow models to correct errors due to discretization and statistical errors. Our method involves fine-tuning the pre-trained flow model using only samples from the data distribution and a simple regularization term that encourages the model to produce samples that are close to the true data distribution. We will evaluate our approach on various real-world benchmarks and compare its performance to other fine-tuning methods.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our method to other fine-tuning methods, such as KL-regularized reward maximization and rejection sampling; ablation study to understand the impact of the regularization term on performance.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to show that our unsupervised fine-tuning approach can improve sample quality and reduce errors in pre-trained flow models, especially for high-dimensional data or when the pre-trained model is imperfect.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Robust Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to use adversarial training to improve the robustness of fine-tuned diffusion models. Specifically, we will train a discriminator to distinguish between real samples from the data distribution and generated samples from the fine-tuned model, and then use this discriminator to regularize the fine-tuning process. We will evaluate the effectiveness of our approach on various real-world benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our method to other fine-tuning methods, such as KL-regularized reward maximization and rejection sampling; ablation study to understand the impact of the adversarial loss on performance.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to show that our adversarial training approach can improve the robustness of fine-tuned diffusion models, especially against adversarial attacks, and provide insights into the trade-off between robustness and sample quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Plug-and-Play Fine-Tuning for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a plug-and-play approach to fine-tuning diffusion models, which allows us to fine-tune a pre-trained diffusion model without modifying its underlying architecture or training procedure. We will evaluate the effectiveness of our approach on various real-world benchmarks and compare its performance to other fine-tuning methods.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our method to other fine-tuning methods, such as KL-regularized reward maximization and rejection sampling; ablation study to understand the impact of the plug-and-play approach on performance.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to show that our plug-and-play approach can simplify the fine-tuning process for diffusion models and provide competitive performance with other fine-tuning methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Evaluation and Comparison of Fine-Tuning Methods for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comprehensive evaluation and comparison of the fine-tuning methods proposed in this research, including KL-regularized reward maximization, multi-step KL regularization, leverage denoising process structure, sequential sampling, unsupervised fine-tuning, adversarial training, and plug-and-play fine-tuning. We will evaluate their performance on various real-world benchmarks and provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each approach.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of each fine-tuning method to the standard diffusion model; ablation study to understand the impact of each fine-tuning method on performance.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to provide a comprehensive understanding of the fine-tuning landscape for diffusion models and guide future research in this area.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of KL Relaxations for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with replacing the intractable marginal KL term with relaxations such as the trajectory KL divergence and evaluate their impact on fine-tuning performance. Specifically, we will fine-tune a pre-trained diffusion model on text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation tasks using PPO with different KL relaxations and compare their performance against a baseline of no KL regularization.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no KL regularization, ablation study: varying the number of timesteps in the trajectory KL relaxation, baseline Reinforcement Learning (RL) method: PPO without KL regularization.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the trajectory KL relaxation to lead to improved stability and performance compared to no KL regularization, but may suffer from the initial value function bias problem.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Regularization via Conditional Reverse Process Matching for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will add an additional regularization term to the KL-regularized reward maximization objective, which encourages the fine-tuned distribution to match the conditional reverse process of the pre-trained model. This regularization can be implemented by minimizing the mutual information between the conditioning variables and the reverse process. We will fine-tune a pre-trained diffusion model on the same tasks as proposal 1 and evaluate the impact of this additional regularization term.
CONTROLS: Ablation study: adding the regularization term with different strengths, baseline: the existing KL relaxation methods from proposal 1.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the added regularization term to mitigate the initial value function bias problem and lead to improved performance, but may introduce additional regularization strength hyperparameters that require tuning.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Exploring Regularization via Conditional Reverse Process Matching for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will refine the proposal by implementing a more efficient way to estimate the mutual information term, using a variational autoencoder (VAE) to approximate the reverse process distribution. This will reduce the computational cost and make the method more scalable.
CONTROLS: Remain the same, with an additional control: comparison against a vanilla VAE.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The efficiency improvement will allow us to consider a larger number of regularization strength hyperparameters, which we expect to lead to even better performance, but also increases the risk of overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning with Flow-Based Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will leverage the generative structure of diffusion models to enforce regularization through a flow-based approach. Specifically, we will insert additional flow layers between the denoising steps to encourage the fine-tuned distribution to be more similar to the pre-trained model's distribution. This proposal explores a novel method to utilize the diffusion model's inherent generative structure for regularization.
CONTROLS: Ablation study: varying the number of flow layers, baseline: the existing KL relaxation methods from proposal 1.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the flow-based regularization to offer improved performance and a more efficient way to enforce regularization, but may require careful tuning of the flow layer architecture.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Exploring Regularization via Conditional Reverse Process Matching for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will incorporate the flow-based regularization idea from proposal 3 into the conditional reverse process matching approach, by using the flow layers to approximate the reverse process distribution. This combined approach will leverage the benefits of both methods, and we will evaluate its performance on the fine-tuning tasks.
CONTROLS: Ablation study: comparing the combined approach against the individual methods from proposals 2 and 3.
COST: 25 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The combination of methods is likely to lead to even better performance, but may also introduce additional hyperparameters that require tuning, and potentially increase the computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-Free Fine-Tuning of Pre-Trained Flow Models
PROPOSAL: We will explore a reward-free fine-tuning approach for pre-trained flow models, where the errors of the pre-trained model are corrected by fine-tuning using only samples from the data distribution, without any explicit reward function. This approach aims to correct for discretization errors and statistical errors in the pre-training process, and we will evaluate its effectiveness on the fine-tuning tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no fine-tuning, ablation study: varying the number of samples used for fine-tuning.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the reward-free fine-tuning approach to lead to improved sample quality, but may require careful tuning of the fine-tuning parameters, and potentially suffer from limited exploration of the model's search space.
